The 2–4 cm Renal Mass

Urologic oncology · small renal mass · teaching pathway

The 2–4 cm renal mass

Who gets pushed to treatment and who stays on surveillance. Five forks for a solid, enhancing cT1a mass in sporadic disease, each with the numbers behind it.

92–95%

of renal cell carcinomas are sporadic. Germline variants account for only 5–8%. Size and outcome figures come from sporadic (the MSKCC surgical series, which includes benign tumours) or unselected registry populations; hereditary data appear only in the syndrome plan at fork 1.NCI PDQ

02

The numbers

Sporadic disease only. Brick bars fall inside this pathway's 2–4 cm scope; hover or tap a bar for its value.

Metastases that developed during surveillance

Surveillance cohorts · cumulative counts

SourceFollow-upMetastases on AS
Smaldone pooled review880 patients, 18 seriesmean 33.5 mo18 (2%)
Jewett 2011178 elderly or frail, Canadian trialmean 28 mo2 (1.1%)
DISSRM intermediate615 patientsmedian 3 yr0
DISSRM, age 60 or under224 patientsmedian 4.9 yr0
Lavallée 20261,393 patients ≤4 cm, Canadian national cohortmedian 4.0 yr29 (2.3% at 5 yr)

In the pooled review, every mass that metastasized was over 3 cm when the metastasis was detected (smallest 3.1 cm, among those with a reported size). Progressors started larger (mean about 4 cm) and grew faster (about 0.8 cm a year), and most with pathology were high grade. The Canadian cohort reports a cumulative incidence of metastasis on AS of 0.67% at 2 years and 2.3% at 5 years. No 10-year figure exists yet.

How often tumours this size had already spread

Metastatic at diagnosis · 2–3 cm vs 3–4 cm · one sporadic surgical series, two unselected registries

Source2–3 cm3–4 cm
MSKCC 20092,691 resected sporadic tumours0.1%all under 3 cm1.8%
SEER 2004–2019181,096 RCCs · clear cell1.5%2.5%
SEER 1988–200422,204 T1 RCCs4.9%7.1%

This is not the risk for a cN0 M0 mass in your clinic. These rates count everyone diagnosed at that size, including patients who were already metastatic and went straight to oncology. All three sources rise at 3 cm. The surgical series counts only patients who had surgery, which leaves out people with metastases managed without it. The SEER 2004–2019 authors found rates roughly two-fold those of nephrectomy cohorts. In the MSKCC series the odds rose 1.25-fold per centimetre.

03

Guidelines side by side

None of the three draws a hard line between 2 and 4 cm. The strength of each statement is shown beneath it where the guideline grades it.

TopicCUA 2022AUA 2021ASCO 2017 (archived)
Under 2 cm
AS is the preferred strategy.Conditional · moderate certainty
AS is an option for initial management.Conditional · Grade C
A mass under 1 cm is a relative indication for AS.
2–4 cm
AS, partial nephrectomy or percutaneous ablation are all options.Conditional · low certainty
Not size-specific: recommend intervention when its oncologic benefit outweighs treatment and competing risks. AS only if the patient accepts the risk.Moderate · Grade C
Partial nephrectomy is the standard when intervention is indicated and the tumour is amenable.
Competing risk
Keep monitoring until oncologic risk rises, the patient chooses treatment, or the benefit of treating comes to outweigh the competing risks.
Prioritize AS when intervention risk or competing mortality outweighs the oncologic benefit.Clinical principle
Absolute indication for AS: life expectancy under 5 years or high procedural risk. Relative: under 10 years, a mass under 1 cm, or significant ESRD risk with treatment.
Biopsy
When the result may change management. Before or at the time of ablation.Expert opinion · expert consensus
When it may change management. Not required for young or healthy patients unwilling to accept its uncertainty, or older or frail patients managed conservatively regardless. Multiple cores over FNA.Expert opinion · Moderate, Grade C
Consider for every small renal mass when the result may alter management.
Ablation
Percutaneous ablation is an option at 2–4 cm. Most data are for tumours under 3 cm; at 3–4 cm, counsel on higher complication and recurrence rates.Conditional · low certainty
Alternate approach for solid cT1a masses under 3 cm, percutaneous preferred.Moderate · Grade CBiopsy before (preferred) or at the time of ablation.Expert opinion
An option if complete ablation can be reliably achieved.
Genetics
Offer counselling when features suggest hereditary RCC.Expert opinion
Recommend counselling for everyone 46 or younger with a renal malignancy, and for multifocal, bilateral or familial disease.Expert opinion
Not addressed in the recommendations summarized here.
Imaging on AS
No consensus on frequency; about every 3–6 months in year one, then every 6–12 months (expert opinion), with ultrasound where it shows the mass well. Chest X-ray until definitive treatment is no longer considered.Chest X-ray: conditional · low certainty
Repeat cross-sectional imaging at about 3–6 months to assess growth; intervene for substantial interval growth.Expert opinion
No formal recommendation. Supporting text: imaging every 3 months in year one, twice in years two and three, then yearly; consider treatment for growth over 0.5 cm a year or size over 4 cm.
04

Weak points

  • There is no randomized trial. DISSRM patients chose their arm, and the AS group was older and sicker with smaller tumours.
  • The horizon is short for young patients. The 60-and-under cohort had a median 4.9 years of follow-up. A 45-year-old carries the mass for 30 years or more.
  • The size data describe presentation, not surveillance. They count metastases at diagnosis, which shows what tumours of a given size can do, not what an M0 mass on AS will do. Below 3 cm the surgical and registry series also disagree by an order of magnitude or more (0.1% against 1.5–4.9%).
  • Biopsy undergrades. At surgery, 16% of low-grade reads were high grade, so a low-grade core lowers the risk without removing it.
  • Growth rate is a weak trigger. In DISSRM it drove most progression calls (2017 report) but did not predict adverse pathology, recurrence or cancer death. Absolute size did.
  • Practice follows the surgeon. In MUSIC, urologists in the bottom quartile of AS use for low-risk prostate cancer put 21% of small renal masses on AS; those in the top quartile put 74%.
  • The leans here are a synthesis. CUA endorses AS or treatment across 2–4 cm on low-certainty evidence. The fork order and the 3 cm split are this pathway's reading of the data above.

    Recommendations and certainty grades match. Biopsy is “prior to, or at the time of” ablation; the AS imaging interval is expert opinion — the panel “was unable to achieve a consensus” on frequency. Ablation evidence is mostly from tumours under 3 cm.

Compiled 7 October 2026 from the sources above. Figures are as reported. Size and outcome data come from sporadic or unselected RCC populations; hereditary data appear only in the syndrome plan. Fork order, leans and the 3 cm split are this pathway's synthesis, built for teaching and case discussion.
